docs.title: dementia-multimodal-ml
docs.text:
Multimodal biostatistics and machine learning for dementia research:

  • MCI-to-dementia conversion on ADNI;
  • open-data Mendelian randomisation of circulating proteins and metabolites on Alzheimer's disease;
  • resting-state EEG classification of AD, FTD and controls;

  • a local tool-using agent over the results.

  • Results

  • Figure index
  • Data sources and ADNI download list
  • Model cards: conversion, EEG, Mendelian randomisation
  • The agent

Source code: https://github.com/mdegiulio97/dementia-multimodal-ml

docs.title: ADNI download list
docs.text:
Tables the owner downloads by hand from LONI IDA (https://ida.loni.usc.edu) into DEMENTIA_ML_DATA/adni/ (default ~/data/dementia-ml/adni/), never inside the repository. Prepared on 2026-11-12 from public ADNI pages; IDA itself was not opened. Rules that apply to these files are in DATA_SOURCES.md, section 5.

Status marks: ✓ verified on a public ADNI page or document, ⚠ name or location from secondary sources (forum, third-party code) and to be confirmed on IDA, ✗ not found.

For every file: keep the original file name, write the download date in DEMENTIA_ML_DATA/adni/DOWNLOADED.txt (<file name> <YYYY-MM-DD>): the DUA requires the download date to be reported in Methods, and the pipelines copy it into provenance.

docs.title: Where things are in IDA ✓
docs.text:
From the ADNI quick-start guide (https://adni.loni.usc.edu/quick-start-guide-asset/getting_started.html and filetour.html): IDA → Search and Download → Study Files (also reachable through the ARC builder). Inside Study Files:

  • Study Info: "Data and database contains a master data dictionary ... This section also includes the necessary files for building the ADNIMERGE package."
  • Biospecimen → Biospecimen Results: laboratory, proteomics and metabolomics tables.
  • Archive: "previous versions of many tables".

Older ADNI news posts give the same path as "DOWNLOAD | Biospecimen | Biospecimen Results".

docs.title: Phase 1 (needed now)
docs.text:
Update 2026-11-13. IDA no longer offers ADNIMERGE.csv. Under Study Info there is only the R package ADNIMERGE2 (ADNIMERGE2.tar.gz, ADNI 1/GO/2/3/4), with CDISC-style tables (ADSL, ADRS, ADQS, plus the source tables). pipelines/prepare_adni.py builds the ADNIMERGE-shaped table from it in Python (pyreadr; R is not needed). Also downloaded: UPENNBIOMK_ROCHE_ELECSYS, BIOMARK, the data dictionary DATADIC, the CruchagaLab SomaScan 7k CSF matrix with its analyte file, and ADNINIGHTINGALE2 with its dictionary.

# File Where in IDA Use Status 1 ADNIMERGE.csv ("ADNIMERGE – Key ADNI tables merged into one table [ADNI1,GO,2,3]") Study Files → Study Info (Data & Database). If it is not there, look under Study Files → Archive MCI-to-AD conversion (Task 3, 5), trajectories (Task 6) ✓ name and existence (ADNI FAQ https://adni.loni.usc.edu/help-faqs/faq/; adni-data group post of 9 Dec 2024 "ADNIMERGE.csv is still available" under "Study Info"); ⚠ a post of 13 Jan 2026 may report a move to Archive, body not readable 2 ADNIMERGE_0.0.1.tar.gz (R package, same data) Study Files → Study Info fallback only, if the CSV is gone; data in data/adnimerge.rdata must be exported with R ✓ name from the package site https://adni.bitbucket.io/index.html 3 Data dictionary (DATADIC / master data dictionary) Study Files → Study Info column definitions, units, codes ✓ existence; ⚠ exact file name 4 DXSUM_PDXCONV_ADNIALL.csv (diagnostic summary) Study Files → Assessments → Diagnosis cross-check of DX and of the conversion date ⚠ name from ADNI expert Q&A (https://adni.loni.usc.edu/experts-knowledge-base/question?QID=1756)

Notes on ADNIMERGE:

  • It covers ADNI1, GO, 2 and 3, not ADNI4 ✓ (FAQ tag "[ADNI1,GO,2,3]"). A successor "including data from ADNI4" is in development ✓ (expert Q&A QID=2019, 29 Oct 2024). An R package called ADNIMERGE2 (v0.1.4, https://atri-biostats.github.io/ADNIMERGE2) is described as available on IDA under Study Files → Study Info → Data & Database ⚠; it is not one merged table but CDISC-style datasets (ADSL, ADQS, ADRS, ...; subject key USUBJID; diagnosis as RSTESTCD == "DX" with CN/MCI/DEM). Phase 1 uses ADNIMERGE.csv; ADNIMERGE2 only if the CSV is unavailable, and then schema.py changes.
  • No official notice that ADNIMERGE is retired was found ⚠.

docs.text:

Column Meaning (package reference) Status RID participant roster id ✓ VISCODE visit code (bl, m06, ...) ✓ EXAMDATE exam date ✓ M "Month since baseline" ✓ (a Month column also exists) DX_bl baseline diagnosis; the R package spells it DX.bl, the CSV DX_bl ✓ DX diagnosis at the visit ✓ AGE age at baseline ✓ PTGENDER sex ✓ PTEDUCAT years of education ✓ APOE4 number of APOE ε4 alleles ✓ MMSE Mini-Mental State Examination ✓ ADAS13 ADAS-Cog 13 ✓ CDRSB CDR sum of boxes ✓ FAQ Functional Activities Questionnaire ✓ Hippocampus "UCSF Hippocampus" volume ✓ ICV "UCSF ICV" ✓ ABETA CSF Aβ ✓ TAU CSF total tau ✓ PTAU CSF p-tau ✓

All 19 are listed (status ✓ = the column name exists). The meanings quoted from the reference are M, Hippocampus, ICV and the "CSF ..." labels of ABETA/TAU/PTAU; the other meanings are the usual reading of the names ⚠, to check in the data dictionary. docs.title: Diagnosis codes
docs.text:
Column Values Status / source DX_bl CN, SMC, EMCI, LMCI, AD, and MCI for ADNI3 recruits ✓ package vignette https://adni.bitbucket.io/articles/Enrollment.html; adni-data group, 5 May 2021; expert Q&A QID=1016: "DX.bl will now have the following categories (CN, SMC, EMCI, LMCI, MCI, AD; where MCI is E- or L- as recruited in ADNI3.)" DX CN, MCI, Dementia ✓ same forum thread; vignette https://adni.bitbucket.io/articles/Longitudinal.html

Consequences for the code:

  • The MCI-at-baseline set must be {"EMCI", "LMCI", "MCI"}, not {"EMCI", "LMCI"} as in the current plan (Task 2 schema.DX_BL_MCI).
  • DX_bl is the screening diagnosis (expert Q&A QID=304) ✓.
  • For ADNI3 rows, DX was at one point filled only at VISCODE == "bl" (QID=1016) ✓. Check the share of missing DX per protocol (COLPROT) before building conversion times; if follow-up DX is missing in ADNI3, derive it from DXSUM_PDXCONV_ADNIALL.csv (DXCHANGE recode {1,7,9} = CN, {2,4,8} = MCI, {3,5,6} = Dementia ✓ from the same Q&A).

docs.title: 1. EEG: OpenNeuro ds004504 ✓
docs.text:
What it is. Resting-state, eyes-closed scalp EEG from 88 people: Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia and cognitively normal controls, recorded at the 2nd Department of Neurology, AHEPA University Hospital, Thessaloniki.

Field Value Status Where it was read URL https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds004504 ✓ OpenNeuro GraphQL https://openneuro.org/crn/graphql Latest version 1.0.9 (snapshot created 2026-05-20); earlier tags 1.0.0 to 1.0.8 (2023-02-17 to 2024-10-30) ✓ GraphQL snapshots, CHANGES Dataset DOI 10.18112/openneuro.ds004504.v1.0.9 ✓ dataset_description.json Descriptor paper DOI 10.3390/data8060095 (Miltiadous et al., Data 2023, 8(6):95, CC BY 4.0) ✓ dataset_description.json, Crossref First study on the data 10.1109/ACCESS.2023.3294618 (DICE-Net, IEEE Access 2023) ✓ HowToAcknowledge, Crossref Benchmark paper 10.1007/s11571-026-10464-w (AHEPA EEG benchmark, Cogn Neurodyn 2026, PMID 42165009) ✓ HowToAcknowledge, Crossref, PubMed License CC0 ✓ dataset_description.json ("License": "CC0") Access open, no registration ✓ anonymous S3 listing and GraphQL worked BIDS version v1.2.1 ✓ dataset_description.json Subjects 88: 36 AD, 29 CN, 23 FTD ✓ counted in participants.tsv; matches README Task eyesclosed; no sessions ✓ GraphQL summary Sampling rate 500 Hz ✓ sub-001_task-eyesclosed_eeg.json (SamplingFrequency) and README Channels 19 EEG: Fp1, Fp2, F3, F4, C3, C4, P3, P4, O1, O2, F7, F8, T3, T4, T5, T6, Fz, Cz, Pz (µV); no EOG/ECG/EMG ✓ sub-001_task-eyesclosed_channels.tsv, eeg.json Reference "EEGReference": "A1 A2" in the sidecar; the README says the referential montage used Cz as common reference and the derivatives were re-referenced to A1-A2 ⚠ the two statements differ; treat the raw reference as uncertain and prefer the derivatives Power-line frequency 50 Hz ✓ eeg.json Recording length about 13.5 min AD (5.1 to 21.3), 12 min FTD (7.9 to 16.9), 13.8 min CN (12.5 to 16.5) ✓ README (sub-001: RecordingDuration 599.8 s) File format EEGLAB .set, data embedded (no .fdt files in the listing) ✓ S3 listing Preprocessed derivatives/ yes: derivatives/sub-XXX/eeg/sub-XXX_task-eyesclosed_eeg.set for all 88 subjects. Pipeline per README: Butterworth band-pass 0.5 to 45 Hz, re-reference to A1-A2, ASR (window SD threshold 17), ICA (RunICA) with ICLabel rejection of eye and jaw components. derivatives/ has no dataset_description.json and no sidecars ✓ S3 listing, README Size snapshot 1.0.9: 2,829,897,704 bytes (raw only, 269 files). Public S3 prefix: 359 objects, 5,780,997,840 bytes in total, of which derivatives/ 2,951,099,688 bytes ✓ GraphQL size; S3 list-type=2 listing summed sha256 not published ✗ OpenNeuro exposes git-annex object ids, not sha256

participants.tsv columns (read on 2026-11-12, 1,706 bytes): participant_id, Gender (M/F), Age (years), Group, MMSE. The Group levels from participants.json:

Code in file Meaning (participants.json) Our label n A Alzheimer Disease Group AD 36 F Frontotemporal Dementia Group FTD 23 C Healthy Group CN 29

Parsing notes: the MMSE cell of sub-050 has a trailing space (30), so strip strings before casting. All CN have MMSE 30 (ceiling), so MMSE must never be used as a feature for CN vs patient tasks (it is the label in disguise).

Download route (free). The public bucket answers anonymous requests:

# whole dataset (about 5.8 GB with derivatives)
aws s3 sync --no-sign-request s3://openneuro.org/ds004504 ./ds004504
# derivatives only (about 2.95 GB) plus the metadata files
aws s3 sync --no-sign-request s3://openneuro.org/ds004504 ./ds004504 \
  --exclude "*" --include "derivatives/*" --include "participants.*" \
  --include "dataset_description.json" --include "README" --include "sub-*/eeg/*.json" \
  --include "sub-*/eeg/*_channels.tsv"

Plain HTTPS works too (https://s3.amazonaws.com/openneuro.org/ds004504/<path>), which is what sources.download can use without the AWS CLI. The S3 bucket holds the current state of the dataset, which today is 1.0.9; for a pinned version use DataLad (datalad install https://github.com/OpenNeuroDatasets/ds004504.git then git checkout 1.0.9) or openneuro-py download --dataset ds004504 --tag 1.0.9. The DataLad and openneuro-py routes were not executed in this session ⚠.

Citation required (HowToAcknowledge): the data descriptor (10.3390/data8060095), the first study (10.1109/ACCESS.2023.3294618) and the AHEPA benchmark (10.1007/s11571-026-10464-w).

docs.title: 2. Alzheimer's disease GWAS: Bellenguez et al. 2022 ✓
docs.text:
What it is. Stage-I genome-wide meta-analysis of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (European ancestry; EADB, GR@CE, EADI, GERAD, PERADES, DemGene, Bonn, RS, CCHS, UK Biobank).

Field Value Status Where it was read Paper Bellenguez C et al. "New insights into the genetic etiology of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias." Nat Genet 2022 Apr ✓ Crossref, PubMed esummary Paper DOI / PMID / PMCID 10.1038/s41588-022-01024-z / 35379992 / PMC9005347; article license CC BY 4.0 ✓ Crossref, PubMed GWAS Catalog accession GCST90027158 (pubmed_id 35379992, trait MONDO_0004975) ✓ https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/rest/api/v2/studies?pubmed_id=35379992 Sample 39,106 clinically diagnosed cases, 46,828 proxy cases, 401,577 controls (European); 21,101,114 variants ✓ GWAS Catalog v2 study record License (summary stats) CC0 1.0 (terms_of_license: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) ✓ GWAS Catalog v2 study record Access open, anonymous FTP/HTTPS ✓ directory listing Folder https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gwas/summary_statistics/GCST90027001-GCST90028000/GCST90027158/ ✓ listing Genome build GRCh38 (genome_assembly: GRCh38, 1-based) ✓ *-meta.yaml

Files in the folder (sizes from HTTP Content-Range, md5 from md5sum.txt; no sha256 is published):

File Bytes md5 Notes harmonised/35379992-GCST90027158-MONDO_0004975.h.tsv.gz 1,140,755,970 e2c8be73b5aa7698c5e8878ae607fe85 chosen: harmonised to Ensembl release 95, is_harmonised: true harmonised/35379992-GCST90027158-MONDO_0004975-Build38.f.tsv.gz 575,146,963 cfd56a310f0ec11846354ddf8a9c5152 formatted, not harmonised GCST90027158_buildGRCh38.tsv.gz 755,201,909 9d23b9ba23532da38ab83fb061bab18f author file, 2025-02-09, is_harmonised: false

Header of the harmonised file (read from the first 16 KB):

hm_variant_id hm_rsid hm_chrom hm_pos hm_other_allele hm_effect_allele hm_beta hm_odds_ratio
hm_ci_lower hm_ci_upper hm_effect_allele_frequency hm_code variant_id p_value chromosome
base_pair_location effect_allele other_allele effect_allele_frequency odds_ratio ci_lower
ci_upper beta standard_error n_cas n_con

Column mapping used by sources.load_outcome_gwas():

Ours File column snp hm_rsid effect_allele hm_effect_allele other_allele hm_other_allele eaf hm_effect_allele_frequency beta hm_beta (log-odds) se standard_error (no harmonised SE; SE does not change sign under allele flipping) pval p_value

Parsing notes, both seen in the bytes read: the harmonised file has Windows line endings (the last field reads n_con\r), so strip \r; for flipped variants hm_beta has the opposite sign of beta (example rs1040232850: beta −0.2494, hm_beta 0.2494).

Caveat for MR: sample overlap. The cohort list includes UK Biobank (proxy cases). The pQTL and mQTL sources below are also UK Biobank based, so exposure and outcome samples overlap in part. Overlap biases two-sample MR towards the confounded observational estimate, with a size that depends on instrument strength (Burgess, Davies & Thompson, Genet Epidemiol 2016, DOI 10.1002/gepi.21998 ✓). It must be stated, and a UK-Biobank-free outcome should be run as sensitivity:

Sensitivity outcome: Kunkle et al. 2019 ⚠. Nat Genet, DOI 10.1038/s41588-019-0358-2, PMID 30820047 ✓; GWAS Catalog GCST007511 (21,982 cases, 41,944 controls, European, no UK Biobank), license "EBI terms of use" ✓. File https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gwas/summary_statistics/GCST007001-GCST008000/GCST007511/Kunkle_etal_Stage1_results.txt, 569,380,789 bytes, space-separated, header Chromosome Position MarkerName Effect_allele Non_Effect_allele Beta SE Pvalue ✓. It has no allele frequency, so palindromic SNPs cannot be resolved from the file and must be dropped. Build not stated in the folder (no meta file) ⚠: positions look like GRCh37 but this was not confirmed. Wightman et al. 2021 (PMID 34493870, GCST013196/GCST013197) also exists in the Catalog but includes UK Biobank as well, so it does not solve the overlap.

docs.title: 3. pQTL exposures: UKB-PPP (Sun et al. 2023), Supplementary Table 9 ✓
docs.text:
Choice and why. It is the lightest open file that has, for each lead pQTL, rsID, both alleles, allele frequency, beta, SE, p and a cis/trans flag, on one platform (Olink Explore) and one cohort, under CC BY 4.0. Per-protein full summary statistics (many GB) are not needed for lead-variant MR.

Field Value Status Paper Sun BB et al. "Plasma proteomic associations with genetics and health in the UK Biobank." Nature 2023 ✓ Crossref DOI / PMID / PMCID 10.1038/s41586-023-06592-6 / 37794186 / PMC10567551; CC BY 4.0 ✓ File 41586_2023_6592_MOESM3_ESM.xlsx ✓ URL https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-023-06592-6/MediaObjects/41586_2023_6592_MOESM3_ESM.xlsx ✓ HTTP 200 Size 34,411,394 bytes ✓ Content-Length sha256 not computed (file read with byte-range requests, not saved) ✗ fill in on first download Sheet ST9 "List of significant (p<1.7e-11) pQTLs in discovery cohort"; header on row 5 ✓ Rows sheet range A1:AF30748, so about 30.7k pQTL rows ⚠ from the stored range, not counted Genome build GRCh37 inside Variant ID, GRCh38 in GENPOS (hg38) ✓ checked rs1260326 against Ensembl

Relevant columns: Variant ID (CHROM:GENPOS (hg37):A0:A1:imp:v1), GENPOS (hg38), UKBPPP ProteinID, Assay Target, Target UniProt, rsID, A1FREQ (discovery), BETA (discovery, wrt. A1), SE (discovery), log10(p) (discovery), cis/trans, cis gene.

Ours File column trait Assay Target snp rsID effect_allele A1 = 4th field of Variant ID other_allele A0 = 3rd field of Variant ID eaf A1FREQ (discovery) beta BETA (discovery, wrt. A1) (per SD of NPX) se SE (discovery) pval 10 ** -log10(p) (discovery): despite the name the column holds −log10(p) (first row 79.24) cis cis/trans == "cis"

Light alternate and test fixture source: Zheng et al. 2020 (Nat Genet, "Phenome-wide Mendelian randomization mapping the influence of the plasma proteome on complex diseases", DOI 10.1038/s41588-020-0682-6, PMID 32895551, PMC7610464 ✓). 41588_2020_682_MOESM3_ESM.xlsx (2,990,385 bytes, sha256 0812c04ca38150e67d6eae1bde3863331ffd61fc0f7634e1120780edd8328a14 ✓), sheet TableS1.Instruments, header row 3, 2,113 instruments for 1,699 proteins (797 cis), columns SNP, Effect_allele, Other_allele, Effect_allele_freq, Beta, SE, P_value, Exposure, Study, Type, Cis/Trans; GRCh37 ✓. Not chosen as primary: instruments are pooled from five studies (rows from Sun, Emilsson, Suhre, Yao, Folkersen) and the article is under Nature terms of use, not CC ⚠. Useful as a known-answer check: its Table S7 reports CD33 (cis instrument rs12459419) against Alzheimer's disease with beta 0.100148, SE 0.018546, colocalised ✓.

Rejected: deCODE (Ferkingstad et al. 2021, DOI 10.1038/s41588-021-00978-w, PMID 34857953): not open access according to Europe PMC, and the supplementary workbook is 44.4 MB.

docs.title: 4. mQTL exposures: Karjalainen et al. 2024, Supplementary Table 5 ✓
docs.text:
Choice and why. NMR metabolomics on the Nightingale platform, the same technology as part of the ADNI metabolomics, CC BY 4.0, and the lead-variant table has every field we need.

Field Value Status Paper Karjalainen MK et al. "Genome-wide characterization of circulating metabolic biomarkers." Nature 2024 ✓ Crossref DOI / PMID / PMCID 10.1038/s41586-024-07148-y / 38448586 / PMC10990933; CC BY 4.0 ✓ File 41586_2024_7148_MOESM6_ESM.xlsx ✓ URL https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-024-07148-y/MediaObjects/41586_2024_7148_MOESM6_ESM.xlsx ✓ HTTP 200 Size 24,669,233 bytes ✓ Content-Length sha256 not computed ✗ fill in on first download Sheet TableS5_all_lead_SNP_assoc, header row 2; trait definitions in TableS2_NMR_traits (233 NMR traits) ✓ Rows range A1:BC8797, about 8,795 lead SNP-trait rows ⚠ from the stored range Genome build GRCh37 (caption: "Genomic positions refer to hg19. Effects are given for allele 1.") ✓ Full summary statistics GWAS Catalog GCST90301941 to GCST90302173, per the data availability statement ⚠ Catalog not queried Ours File column trait Metabolite (short codes such as Ala) snp Rsid effect_allele Allele1 (lower case: upper-case it) other_allele Allele2 (lower case) eaf Freq1 beta Effect se StdErr pval P-value

There is no cis/trans flag (not meaningful for most metabolites), so the cis-only rule of Task 8 applies to proteins only. Whether the meta-analysis includes UK Biobank participants was not checked ⚠; assume overlap with the outcome GWAS until checked.

Not used: OpenGWAS. Most endpoints of https://api.opengwas.io/api/ now need a token ("The token is required for most endpoints") ✓, so it is not a zero-setup route.

docs.title: 5. ADNI
docs.text:
What it is. Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative: longitudinal multi-site cohort (CN, MCI, AD) with clinical, cognitive, imaging, CSF/plasma, genetic and omics data, distributed by LONI IDA after an approved application.

Field Value Status URL https://adni.loni.usc.edu (data through https://ida.loni.usc.edu) ✓ Access Data Use Agreement (DUA); the owner's access is active ✓ Current DUA https://adni.loni.usc.edu/wp-content/themes/adni_2023/documents/ADNI_Data_Use_Agreement.pdf (the "ADNI Data Use Agreement" link in the site footer; no revision date printed; includes an Appendix A on AI tools) ✓ Older DUA / policy https://adni.loni.usc.edu/wp-content/uploads/how_to_apply/ADNI_Data_Use_Agreement.pdf (Rev December 20, 2016); https://adni.loni.usc.edu/wp-content/uploads/how_to_apply/ADNI_DSP_Policy.pdf (Rev April 3, 2024) ✓ Citation guide https://adni.loni.usc.edu/wp-content/uploads/how_to_apply/ADNI_Manuscript_Citations.pdf (Rev January 28, 2016; its funding text is out of date, use the DUA text) ✓ Tables to download docs/ADNI_DOWNLOAD_LIST.md ⚠ file names partly from third-party code

docs.title: 5.1 What the DUA says (quotes from the current DUA unless noted)
docs.text:
Individual-level data: redistribution is forbidden ✓.

"I will not further disclose these data beyond the uses outlined in this agreement and my data use application. I understand that redistribution of individual participant-level data in any manner is prohibited. Reports and publication of summary (not participant-level) data are allowed." (term 3)

"I will not disclose any participant-level raw or derived datasets beyond the uses outlined in this agreement. ... I understand derived datasets should only be shared through the ADNI-LONI and/or other NIA-designated data repository." (term 5)

"I understand that I am not allowed to distribute ADNI data outside of my team, only the ADNI study website operated by LONI-IDA can distribute data." (term 6)

Review by the Data and Publications Committee (DPC) ✓: required for manuscripts.

"I will submit all manuscripts to the ADNI Data and Publications Committee (DPC) prior to submitting them to a journal. This review will not be a scientific review, but it is intended to ensure that the items above are correctly implemented. ... will complete its review within 2 weeks."

The DSP Policy adds: "The ADNI DPC will not attempt to evaluate the scientific merit of proposed analyses, nor evaluate proposed abstracts. The DPC will be charged with the administrative review of manuscripts only." Submission route: IDA "My Account" → "Update" on the ADNI project → "Publication Update" tab, then e-mail the manuscript to the DPC (address in the DUA).

Trained models ✓ (Appendix A).

"investigators who intend on making the weights of a trained model publicly available should consider whether the model could be used to easily reconstruct parts of the ADNI data set. ADNI prohibits release of participant level data, even if it is sufficiently processed or altered and lack ADNI subject codes."

AI tools ✓ (term 4, Appendix A). ADNI data may not be put into third-party AI tools that keep or reuse inputs, including "inclusion of ADNI data as part of an input or 'prompt' for a generative language model"; "opt-out" clauses are not "an acceptable safeguard". The exception is tools "developed and internally trained by individual research groups ... strictly used for the individual research group" with guaranteed containment.

Data version ✓. "I will note the version (download date) of the data I download and provide this information in any Methods section".

Small cells ✗. No minimum cell size is stated in the DUA, the DSP Policy or the citation guide. The agent's refusal below N = 10 is this project's own rule.

docs.title: 5.2 Answer: can ADNI aggregates go on a public GitHub repository without DPC review? ⚠
docs.text:
• Summary results are explicitly allowed (term 3: "Reports and publication of summary (not participant-level) data are allowed").
  • DPC pre-review is required for "manuscripts" before journal submission. No clause mentions websites, code repositories or software, so the DUA neither requires nor waives DPC review for a GitHub README with aggregate tables and figures. This is an inference from silence, not an explicit permission.
  • Individual-level data, raw or derived, must never be published, and this extends to anything that could reconstruct it: per-subject out-of-fold predictions and trained model files (a random survival forest stores training samples in its leaves).

Conservative route if the owner sets publish_adni_aggregates: true: publish only aggregate metrics and figures (no per-subject points), with the acknowledgement text and the ADNIMERGE download date in the README; keep models/adni/ and conversion_predictions.parquet local; optionally notify the DPC through the IDA "Publication Update" route; any later manuscript goes through the DPC as required.

Owner decision (2026-11-12): the conservative route. ADNI conversion results will be published as aggregate tables and figures only, with the acknowledgement below and the ADNIMERGE download date; models and per-participant predictions stay local. publish_adni_aggregates is set to true in the same commit that adds the first ADNI aggregates.

All three are PubMed records read on 2026-11-12; numbers are quoted from the abstracts.

docs.text: Every figure in the repository, what it shows and what to take from it. Figures under figures/synthetic/ come from the synthetic ADNIMERGE-shaped cohort (a method check with a known answer, not a clinical result). Figures under figures/open/ come from real open data. docs.title: figures/synthetic/conversion_cindex_forest.png
docs.text: Harrell's C-index of the four survival models, computed on out-of-fold predictions (5-fold cross-validation split by participant) with 95% bootstrap intervals. The baseline uses age, MMSE and APOE4 only. In the synthetic cohort the true hazard depends on APOE4, MMSE, ADAS13 and ICV-adjusted hippocampal volume, so the full Cox model should beat the baseline and the flexible models should not do better than the correctly specified Cox model. Both happen (0.72 vs 0.64), which is the check the figure exists for.

docs.title: figures/synthetic/conversion_km_by_risk_tertile.png
docs.text: Kaplan-Meier cumulative conversion for participants grouped by tertile of out-of-fold risk from the best model. Separation between the curves is what a C-index summarises; the high-risk third converts several times more often than the low-risk third over four years.

docs.title: figures/synthetic/conversion_calibration_36m.png
docs.text: Predicted vs observed (Kaplan-Meier) probability of conversion by 36 months, by fifth of predicted risk. Points on the diagonal mean the predicted probabilities can be read as probabilities, not only as rankings.

docs.title: figures/synthetic/trajectories_MMSE.png
docs.text: Mean MMSE trajectory with 95% confidence band from a linear mixed model (random intercept and slope per participant), converters vs stable MCI. The synthetic cohort was generated with a 1.5 points/year faster decline in converters; the model estimates 1.15/year, lower because "converter" is defined from observed follow-up while the simulated decline uses the latent conversion time.

docs.title: figures/synthetic/trajectories_ADAS13.png

The known slowing of the EEG in Alzheimer's disease is visible as more theta and less alpha in AD than in controls; FTD sits in between. Each number below comes from a result file in results/ that records its own provenance (dataset version or checksum, git commit, configuration, seed). Comparisons with published work cite only papers whose records were checked (see DATA_SOURCES.md, section 6).

Marks: ✓ consistent with the reference; ⚠ consistent with caveats; ✗ inconsistent.

docs.title: Resting-state EEG: AD, FTD and controls (OpenNeuro ds004504)
docs.text:
88 participants, 34,788 four-second epochs. All metrics are per participant and come from 5 × 5-fold CV split by participant, with 95% bootstrap intervals. The intervals resample participants over pooled out-of-fold predictions, so they do not include the variance from refitting the models.

Task n Model AUC Balanced accuracy AD vs CN 65 logistic 0.91 (0.82-0.97) 0.81 (0.70-0.91) AD vs CN 65 LightGBM 0.90 (0.81-0.97) 0.81 (0.70-0.91) FTD vs CN 52 logistic 0.74 (0.59-0.87) 0.65 (0.53-0.76) FTD vs CN 52 LightGBM 0.83 (0.70-0.94) 0.73 (0.61-0.84) AD vs FTD 59 logistic 0.61 (0.44-0.76) 0.57 (0.48-0.66) AD vs FTD 59 LightGBM 0.53 (0.36-0.69) 0.59 (0.51-0.69) 3-class 88 LightGBM 0.74 (0.66-0.82) (one-vs-rest) 0.63 (0.54-0.71)

Comparison with the literature. The AHEPA benchmark (Miltiadous et al. 2026, doi:10.1007/s11571-026-10464-w) averages the 12 subject-level studies on this dataset.

  • AD vs CN ✓. The benchmark reports 82.1% accuracy, and our balanced accuracy is 0.81. Mlinarič et al. 2026 (doi:10.1038/s41598-026-35316-9, leave-one-subject-out) report ROC-AUC 0.82; we get 0.90-0.91.
  • FTD vs CN ✓. The benchmark reports 75.2% accuracy; our balanced accuracy is 0.73 with LightGBM.
  • AD vs FTD ⚠. The benchmark reports 71.4% accuracy, but that number disagrees with its own table. Mlinarič report AUC 0.65. We are close to chance.

Studies that let epochs of one person cross folds report 9-17 points more. The benchmark names this leakage as the reason; our splits exclude it by construction and a test checks it.

Limitations. - One small single-centre dataset, with no external test set. - We used the preprocessing shipped with the dataset. - In these recordings most power lies below 2 Hz, so relative delta power is about 0.88 in every group. The spectrum of two controls was checked and the dominance is a property of the data, not a computation error. Phase 2 adds a sensitivity analysis with delta at 1-4 Hz.

docs.title: Sensitivity analyses and deep learning (phase 2)
docs.text:
Delta from 1 Hz instead of 0.5 Hz. The results do not change.

Task Model AUC, 0.5-45 Hz AUC, 1-45 Hz AD vs CN logistic 0.91 0.90 (0.81-0.97) AD vs CN LightGBM 0.90 0.90 (0.80-0.97) FTD vs CN logistic 0.74 0.76 (0.60-0.88) FTD vs CN LightGBM 0.83 0.83 (0.70-0.94)

Even from 1 Hz, delta keeps about 80% of the relative power in every group (medians 0.80-0.82). The slow-activity dominance is a property of these recordings, not of the band edge.

EEGNet on raw 4-s windows (125 Hz, z-scored per channel). It uses the same outer folds by participant, early stopping on an inner split that is also by participant, and one prediction per participant.

Task n EEGNet AUC EEGNet balanced accuracy Best spectral model AUC AD vs CN 65 (13,282 windows) 0.81 (0.69-0.90) 0.63 (0.53-0.73) 0.91 FTD vs CN 52 (10,152 windows) 0.64 (0.48-0.78) 0.56 (0.46-0.66) 0.83

With 52-65 participants, the convolutional network does worse than spectral features. Its training loss falls from 0.63 to 0.17, while performance on held-out participants stays below the spectral models. The network fits the participants it has seen. Thousands of windows do not make up for few people, because the windows of one person are not independent examples. This is the expected behaviour of deep learning on small clinical cohorts, and it is why the spectral models remain the primary EEG result.

docs.title: Mendelian randomisation: circulating proteins and metabolites on Alzheimer's disease
docs.text:
Inputs. - Exposures: UKB-PPP cis-pQTL (Sun et al. 2023, doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06592-6) and NMR metabolite QTL (Karjalainen et al. 2024, doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07148-y). - Outcome: Bellenguez et al. 2022 (doi:10.1038/s41588-022-01024-z, GCST90027158).

Instruments. We excluded the APOE region and pruned to one variant per 500 kb.

Family Tested FDR < 0.05 Selected for ADNI Proteins (cis-pQTL) 1,584 44 44 Metabolites (NMR) 233 7 6

Strongest protein signals. CR1, TREM2, PILRA/PILRB, CD2AP, GRN, EPHA1, ACE, CD55, CD33 and others. - Most of these sit in known AD GWAS loci. That is expected, because a cis-pQTL at a GWAS locus gives a strong Wald ratio. - It is also the main caveat: without colocalisation, the protein and the disease may share a locus without sharing a causal variant. - The full table is results/open/mr_candidates.csv, and the list passed to ADNI is results/open/mr_candidates_selected.txt.

Metabolites. The seven FDR-significant traits are lipoprotein composition measures and glutamine, each with 18-47 instruments, so the sensitivity estimators apply. Six (Gln, L-VLDL-TG%, M-LDL-FC%, M-LDL-PL%, XS-VLDL-FC, XXL-VLDL-CE%) are passed to ADNI. L-VLDL-C% is held back because its Egger intercept is borderline (p = 0.049).

Known-answer check ✓. For CD33 we estimate +0.032 log-odds of AD per SD (95% CI 0.017-0.047). This is the same direction as the colocalised estimate in Zheng et al. 2020 (doi:10.1038/s41588-020-0682-6, Table S7: +0.100). The magnitudes differ because the studies use different pQTL sources, outcome GWAS and scaling.

Sensitivity: an AD GWAS without UK Biobank ✓. UK Biobank is in both the pQTL study and Bellenguez 2022, so the screen was repeated with Kunkle et al. 2019 (doi:10.1038/s41588-019-0358-2, GCST007511, no UK Biobank). - Kunkle has no allele frequencies, so every palindromic instrument is dropped (1,100). - Of the 50 selected molecules, 45 could be tested: - 42 keep the same sign, and 26 of them reach p < 0.05; - FES, ARHGAP45 and LRP11 change sign, all with Kunkle p > 0.3; - TREM2, CD2AP, F13B, FCRLB and SULT1A1 have no usable instrument. - Nine proteins pass FDR with Kunkle: CR1, EPHA1, CELA2A, PILRA, PILRB, C1S, C1R, CD33 and IL34. All but CELA2A were already selected. - Across all 1,465 traits tested with both outcomes, the estimates correlate at r = 0.42, mostly noise around zero; the selected molecules sit along the diagonal (figures/open/mr_bellenguez_vs_kunkle.png).

The sample overlap therefore does not create the signal: the selected molecules keep their direction in an independent GWAS.

Colocalisation of the strongest candidates ✓/⚠. The question is whether the protein and AD share the same causal variant. If they do not, the MR signal could come from linkage disequilibrium with a different variant.

Method. coloc ABF (Giambartolomei et al. 2014, doi:10.1371/journal.pgen.1004383): priors p1 = p2 = 1e-4 and p12 = 1e-5, a ±500 kb window around the cis lead variant, UKB-PPP European discovery regional summary statistics against Bellenguez 2022 (GRCh38). It was run on the nine candidates that held up with Kunkle 2019.

Protein Variants PP.H4 (shared) PP.H3 (distinct) CR1 4,261 0.996 0.004 PILRA 3,253 0.995 0.005 PILRB 3,251 0.995 0.005 IL34 2,629 0.970 0.025 C1S 3,958 0.961 0.033 CD33 5,555 0.953 0.024 C1R 3,978 0.939 0.051 EPHA1 2,549 0.016 0.984 ACE 3,227 0.001 0.999
  • Seven proteins colocalise strongly (PP.H4 > 0.93): CR1, PILRA/PILRB, IL34, C1S/C1R and CD33.
  • CD33 matches the known answer ✓. Zheng et al. 2020 also report CD33 as colocalised.
  • ACE and EPHA1 do not colocalise under ABF, which assumes one causal variant per trait. The two loci were therefore re-analysed with SuSiE (below).

SuSiE-based colocalisation for ACE and EPHA1.

Method. - Fine-mapping with SuSiE-RSS (Zou et al. 2022, doi:10.1371/journal.pgen.1010299; L = 10) for each trait. - The LD comes from UK Biobank (Alkes Price group, s3://broad-alkesgroup-ukbb-ld, GRCh37), the same population as UKB-PPP. - Colocalisation is computed for every pair of credible sets (Wallace 2021, doi:10.1371/journal.pgen.1009440). - Implemented in Python in dementia_ml.mr.susie and tested on simulated loci with a known answer.

Protein Variants Credible sets (protein / AD) Best PP.H4 MR, strongest pQTL MR, colocalising signal ACE 3,072 5 / 1 0.98 −0.12 (SE 0.018) −0.19 (−0.24 to −0.14), p = 2×10⁻¹⁵ EPHA1 2,417 10 / 1 0.008 −0.29 (SE 0.043) none
  • ACE colocalises ✓. The ACE locus carries five independent signals for plasma ACE. One of them, not the strongest, is shared with AD (PP.H4 = 0.98). The ABF result was an artefact of its single-variant assumption.
  • Corrected ACE estimate. The first MR estimate used the strongest pQTL, which is not the AD signal. With the colocalising variant as instrument (17:61548948 C/A, GRCh37) the estimate is −0.19 log-odds of AD per SD of plasma ACE, stronger than before and in the same direction. It is also the same direction as in ADNI CSF, where higher ACE predicts lower conversion (HR 0.76).
  • EPHA1 does not colocalise ✗, even with multiple signals allowed. Its MR signal most likely reflects LD with a different causal variant, so EPHA1 is no longer counted among the credible candidates.
  • Caveat ⚠. Ten credible sets for EPHA1 at n ≈ 34,000 point to sensitivity to small LD differences. The reference is UK Biobank, as are the pQTLs, which limits this.

Epitope-effect check ⚠. A variant that changes the protein sequence can change how the Olink antibody binds the protein without changing its amount. In that case the cis-pQTL partly measures binding, not abundance.

Method. For each colocalised protein, the instrument and its 1000 Genomes EUR proxies (r² ≥ 0.8) were annotated with Ensembl VEP. Protein-altering means missense, stop, start-lost, frameshift, in-frame indel or a splice donor/acceptor variant in the gene encoding the protein.

Protein Instrument Proxies (r² ≥ 0.8) Result ACE (colocalising signal) rs4459609 9 no protein-altering variant ✓ C1R rs10849546 16 no protein-altering variant ✓ PILRB rs1859788 7 none in PILRB ✓, but the same variant is missense in PILRA ⚠ PILRA rs1859788 7 instrument is missense ⚠ IL34 rs4985556 1 instrument is missense ⚠ C1S rs12146727 16 instrument is missense ⚠ CD33 rs2455069 13 instrument is missense ⚠ CR1 rs679515 21 two protein-altering proxies (rs2296160, rs4844600) ⚠

For five of the eight proteins the pQTL may partly reflect antibody binding. The colocalisation still holds: the variant is shared with AD. What weakens is the step from "this variant" to "the amount of this protein". A protein-altering variant can also be truly functional, and this check cannot tell the two apart. ACE and C1R are clean.

ACE is the only candidate supported by four independent checks: 1. MR with a colocalising instrument; 2. colocalisation of a shared variant; 3. no protein-altering variant in LD with the instrument; 4. the same direction in CSF in an independent cohort (ADNI).

Correcting a harmonisation bug mattered. An earlier version flipped the sign of palindromic instruments (A/T, C/G) whose alleles were listed in the opposite order. This corrupted the multi-instrument metabolite estimates (0 significant before the fix, 7 after), while the single-instrument protein results stayed the same. Tests now cover both orderings and the strand flip.

Excluding the APOE region mattered. In the first run, proteins next to APOE (BCAM, NECTIN2, PVR, CEACAM19) passed FDR. They disappear once APOE-region instruments are dropped, as they should if APOE drives them.

Limitations. - Almost every protein has one instrument, so Egger and the weighted median cannot be estimated. - There is no colocalisation. - UK Biobank is in both the exposure and the outcome GWAS (sample overlap). - Pruning is by distance, not by LD.

docs.text:
The synthetic cohort has 1,500 participants with an ADNIMERGE-like structure. Of these, 787 had MCI at baseline with follow-up, and 225 converted. They are generated from a known Weibull hazard. The metrics are out-of-fold, from 5-fold CV split by participant.

What should happen does happen: - The full model beats the baseline, because the simulated hazard uses ADAS13 and hippocampal volume. - The correctly specified Cox model is not beaten by the flexible models. - Calibration at 36 months follows the diagonal. - The Cox coefficients recover the simulated log hazard ratios within ±0.15 (test).

The 48-month horizon is skipped because it equals the end of follow-up.

Reference for the real-data run. Wang et al. 2023 (doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2023.03.009) is the closest design: ADNI MCI, Cox, 10-fold CV, c-index 0.74 (0.70-0.79). Published values on ADNI span 0.68 to 0.90, the higher values with richer feature sets.

docs.text: Mixed model with random intercept and slope: - MMSE declines 1.15 points/year faster in converters (95% CI 1.06-1.24). - ADAS13 worsens 1.77 points/year faster (1.62-1.92).

docs.title: ADNI results
docs.text:
Aggregate results on ADNI (ADNI 1, GO, 2, 3 and 4), published as summary data under the ADNI Data Use Agreement. Models, per-participant predictions and the ADNI table stay local.

Data. - The ADNIMERGE2 R package, downloaded from LONI IDA on 2026-11-13. ADNIMERGE2 replaces the old single ADNIMERGE.csv; pipelines/prepare_adni.py rebuilds the table from its ADSL, ADRS and ADQS tables. - Hippocampal and intracranial volumes from FreeSurfer, ComBat-harmonised across scanners (ADSP_PHC_T1_FS). - CSF Aβ42, t-tau and p-tau181 from Roche Elecsys (UPENN). - Imaging and CSF are the record closest to enrolment, within 180 days.

Cohort. - 1,271 participants had MCI at baseline. 125 had no follow-up diagnosis and were excluded, which leaves 1,146 participants and 420 conversions to dementia. - Observed at baseline: hippocampal volume for 1,061, CSF for 716, APOE for 1,135.

Model Harrell's C Uno's C (36 m) td-AUC 24 m td-AUC 36 m td-AUC 48 m Cox, age + MMSE + APOE4 0.69 (0.67-0.72) 0.69 (0.66-0.72) 0.72 0.74 0.77 Cox (ridge), all baseline 0.83 (0.81-0.85) 0.83 (0.81-0.85) 0.86 0.89 0.90 Random survival forest 0.83 (0.81-0.85) 0.83 (0.81-0.85) 0.86 0.88 0.89 Gradient-boosted survival 0.83 (0.81-0.85) 0.84 (0.82-0.85) 0.87 0.89 0.89

Calibration. Predicted conversion by 36 months follows the observed (Kaplan-Meier) one across fifths of risk: 0.05/0.00, 0.10/0.08, 0.20/0.22, 0.44/0.49, 0.77/0.75, with about 230 participants per fifth.

Comparison ✓. Wang et al. 2023 (doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2023.03.009) report a c-index of 0.74 with clinical variables. Saeed et al. 2024 (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0314725) report 0.82-0.90 with multimodal random survival forests. Our clinical baseline (0.69) and full models (0.83) sit inside that range.

The three flexible and linear models reach the same discrimination. A ridge Cox model on baseline values is as good as the forests here, so it stays the model behind the agent.

Caveat ⚠. CDR-SB and FAQ measure daily function, and functional impairment is part of the clinical definition of dementia. Part of their predictive weight is therefore built into the outcome. The baseline model without them (0.69) is the honest lower bound.

Do the MR candidates predict conversion in ADNI? Mostly no. Each molecule measured at baseline (within 180 days of enrolment) was tested in its own Cox model of conversion. The molecule was inverse-normal transformed, so hazard ratios are per SD, and each model was adjusted for age, sex and APOE4. FDR was computed across all molecules of each platform.

Platform MCI participants (conversions) Molecules tested FDR < 0.05 MR candidates measured Candidates at p < 0.05 Enrichment vs other molecules Same direction as MR CSF proteins, SomaScan 7k (CruchagaLab) 389 (170) 7,008 aptamers 81 (78 genes) 37 genes, 48 aptamers 4 / 48 (others: 12%) Mann-Whitney p = 0.49 19 / 48 Serum NMR metabolites (ADMC Nightingale) 786 (342) 250 0 6 0 / 6 (others: 14%) p = 0.98 4 / 6
  • The screen does detect signal. The CSF proteins most associated with conversion are markers of neuronal and synaptic injury: the 14-3-3 family (YWHAG, YWHAZ, YWHAB, YWHAE) and neurofilament heavy chain (NEFH), with HR 1.5-1.8 per SD. They act as a positive control for the pipeline.
  • The candidates do not stand out. Taken together, the 48 aptamers of the MR candidates are no more associated with conversion than the rest of the proteome. Their direction agrees with MR in 19 of 48, which is chance level.
  • ACE is the exception ✓. Higher CSF ACE predicts lower conversion: HR 0.76 per SD, p = 0.0006, which survives Bonferroni across the 48 candidate aptamers. MR points the same way: genetically higher ACE means lower AD risk.
  • Two discordant candidates. CD2AP (HR 0.80) and ACHE (HR 1.28) are nominally associated in the direction opposite to MR.

Why a negative result is plausible ⚠. Several differences separate the two analyses: - Tissue. MR used plasma protein levels; ADNI measures CSF. - Question. MR asks about lifetime risk of AD; ADNI asks about progression from MCI over a few years, a stage where markers of ongoing injury dominate. - Instruments. Most MR hits rest on a single cis variant at a known GWAS locus, without colocalisation. - Power. 389 participants detect only fairly large effects.

So the MR candidates are not validated as markers of progression; ACE is the one worth following up. Full tables: results/adni_public/omics_proteins.csv and omics_metabolites.csv.

Multimodal fusion: what do biomarkers add to the clinical prediction?

Blocks. - Clinical: age, education, APOE4, MMSE, ADAS13, CDR-SB, FAQ. - MRI: hippocampus and ICV, plus regional FreeSurfer volumes (amygdala, ventricles) and the thickness of seven AD-signature regions. - CSF: Aβ42, t-tau, p-tau. - CSF proteomics: SomaScan 7k, reduced to 20 principal components. - Serum metabolomics: NMR, reduced to 10 components.

Method. - Imputation, scaling and PCA are fitted inside each training fold. - Participants without a block get zeros for it, plus an indicator. This way all 1,146 participants are kept, although only 389 have proteomics and 785 have metabolomics. - Differences against the clinical model come from a paired bootstrap on the same participants.

Blocks C-index, ridge Cox C-index, boosted Difference vs clinical (Cox; boosted) Baseline (age, MMSE, APOE4) 0.69 (0.67-0.72) 0.70 (0.67-0.72) −0.12; −0.13 Clinical 0.82 (0.80-0.83) 0.82 (0.81-0.84) — + hippocampus 0.82 0.83 +0.005 (−0.003, +0.013); +0.004 + regional MRI 0.83 0.83 +0.010 (−0.001, +0.019); +0.011 (+0.001, +0.019) + CSF 0.82 0.83 +0.006; +0.006 (both CIs include 0) + proteomics 0.82 0.83 0.000; +0.003 (both include 0) + metabolomics 0.82 0.82 +0.004; +0.001 (both include 0) All blocks 0.83 (0.82-0.85) 0.84 (0.82-0.86) +0.018 (+0.006, +0.030); +0.016 (+0.005, +0.025) Baseline + biomarkers (no CDR-SB, FAQ) 0.79 (0.76-0.81) 0.78 (0.75-0.80) −0.028; −0.046
  • Clinical scales carry most of the information. All biomarkers together add about 0.02 in C-index, which is real but small. Regional MRI is the single block that comes closest to adding something on its own.
  • The biology is there, but it overlaps with the clinical scales. Without CDR-SB and FAQ, biomarkers raise the baseline from 0.69 to 0.79. This answers the circularity caveat above: the biomarkers predict conversion independently of the functional scales, but they add little once those scales are known.
  • Complete-case check ⚠. Among the 358 participants with every block, all data together reach 0.81 (0.77-0.84), the same as the clinical model (0.81). The small gain of the full cohort does not show up in this subset.

Cognitive trajectories (mixed model, 1,146 participants). Converters decline faster than stable MCI: - MMSE: 1.27 points/year faster (1.15-1.39); - ADAS13: 2.85 points/year faster (2.57-3.14); - CDR-SB: 1.07 points/year faster (1.00-1.15).

Data used in the preparation of these results were obtained from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database (adni.loni.usc.edu); see the acknowledgement in the README.

docs.text: The same code runs locally on ADNIMERGE. ADNI results will be added here as aggregate tables and figures only, with no per-participant data, as the ADNI Data Use Agreement allows. Trained ADNI models and per-participant predictions always stay in the gitignored results/adni/ and models/.

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
Tool selection by the local model qwen2.5:7b-instruct (Ollama, CPU) on the 12 golden questions: 11/12 (run on 2026-11-12; median 40 s per question on CPU).

  • The miss. "How much faster does MMSE decline in converters?" went to cohort_summary instead of get_result("trajectories"). The model wrote the variable in lower case, the tool refused it, and the agent returned the refusal rather than a number.
  • Correct answers. Risk questions were answered with the tool's probability and bootstrap interval, for example "31.5% (28.1%-36.1%) at 3 years" for a synthetic profile. The request for a single participant's MMSE was refused.

In CI, a scripted backend checks routing, refusals (small cells, participant identifiers), provenance and abstention on every run.

docs.title: The local analysis agent
docs.text: The agent answers questions about this project's data and results without inventing numbers. A local model, served by Ollama, chooses which tool to call. The tools do the computing and return a value together with its uncertainty and provenance. The model only words the answer.

docs.title: Why tools and not a fine-tuned model
docs.text: A language model trained on participant data can memorise it, which is both a privacy problem and a breach of the ADNI Data Use Agreement. A model that recalls numbers from its weights also gets them wrong. Here the model is never trained on the data: everything it "knows" about the data reaches it through the tool results.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: Tool Returns Guards describe_data sources, cohort sizes, variables, available results none needed cohort_summary(filters, variable) n, mean and SD (one decimal) of a baseline variable in the MCI cohort; quartiles only from n ≥ 20 categorical filters only (APOE4, converted, age band); refuses N < 10; refuses a cell whose sibling (one filter dropped) holds 1-9 people, so two answers cannot be subtracted down to a small group; refuses participant IDs predict_conversion_risk(age, mmse, apoe4, ..., horizon_months) conversion probability from the full Cox model, with a 95% interval from 50 bootstrap refits warns when inputs fall outside the training 1st-99th percentiles (never min/max, which are individual values), caps the horizon at the end of follow-up, lists imputed features explain_prediction(...) per-feature contributions to the log hazard (exact linear SHAP) none needed get_result(name) stored results: conversion_metrics, trajectories, mr_candidates, eeg_metrics unknown names refused

docs.title: Abstention
docs.text: If no tool returned a value, because nothing was called, the request was refused or the tool was unknown, the agent abstains and replaces whatever the model wrote with a fixed message. If the answer contains a number that matches no tool value, it is withheld too, and the raw tool results are shown instead. A number counts as matched when it equals a tool value (or that value as a percentage) at the precision written, or when it appears in the question. The check works on numbers, so a wrong claim written in words would not be caught.

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text:
src/dementia_ml/agent/golden.yaml holds 12 questions with the tool that must answer each one, including a request for a single participant that must be refused.

  • In CI: a scripted backend checks routing, refusals, provenance and abstention.
  • Locally: uv run pytest -m ollama checks that the live model calls the expected tool in at least 80% of the questions. The measured rate is in RESULTS.md.

docs.title: MCP
docs.text: uv run --extra mcp dementia-mcp serves the same tools over stdio, so any Model Context Protocol client gets the same refusals and provenance. MCP clients are often driven by cloud models, so ADNI mode is refused unless started with --kind adni --allow-adni-to-client, which is meant only for a client backed by a local model.

docs.title: Model card: MCI-to-dementia conversion
docs.text:
Task. Predict time from a baseline visit with mild cognitive impairment (ADNI DX_bl in EMCI, LMCI or MCI) to the first visit with a dementia diagnosis.

Data. ADNIMERGE (ADNI 1, GO, 2, 3), run locally under the ADNI Data Use Agreement. The public repository runs the same code on a synthetic cohort with the ADNIMERGE schema.

Outcome definition. Event: first follow-up visit with DX == "Dementia" (later reversions ignored). Censoring: last follow-up visit with a recorded diagnosis. Participants with no follow-up diagnosis are excluded and counted.

Features. Baseline values only: age, MMSE, APOE4 count (baseline model); plus education, ADAS13, CDR-SB, FAQ, hippocampal volume adjusted for intracranial volume, CSF Aβ42, t-tau, p-tau (full models). CSF values reported at assay limits (">1700", "<8") are set to the limit with a flag.

Models. Cox (age + MMSE + APOE4); ridge-penalised Cox on all features; random survival forest; gradient-boosted survival trees. Preprocessing (hippocampus residualisation on ICV, median imputation with missingness indicators, scaling) is fitted inside each training fold.

Validation. 5-fold cross-validation split by participant and stratified by event; metrics on pooled out-of-fold predictions with 1000-sample participant bootstrap: Harrell's C, Uno's C at 36 months, time-dependent AUC at 24/36/48 months, calibration at 36 months. Horizons at or beyond the last follow-up are skipped and reported.

Synthetic check. Full Cox C = 0.72 (0.68-0.76) vs baseline 0.64 (0.60-0.68); the Cox coefficients recover the simulated log hazard ratios within ±0.15 (tests/data).

ADNI. 1,146 participants with MCI and 420 conversions. The full models reach C 0.83 (0.81-0.85), the clinical baseline C 0.69 (0.67-0.72), with good calibration at 36 months. Data come from ADNIMERGE2 through data/adnimerge2.py. Imaging and CSF are taken within 180 days of enrolment.

Intended use. Research on prognostic modelling methods. Not a clinical tool.

Known limitations. Interval censoring at visit times is treated as exact; competing risk of death is not modelled; ADNI is a volunteer research cohort, not a clinical population.

Not published. Trained ADNI models and per-participant predictions (DUA, Appendix A).

docs.title: Model card: resting-state EEG classification
docs.text:
Task. Classify participants as Alzheimer's disease (AD), frontotemporal dementia (FTD) or healthy control (CN) from eyes-closed resting EEG. Four tasks: AD vs CN, FTD vs CN, AD vs FTD, three-class.

Data. OpenNeuro ds004504 v1.0.9 (CC0): 88 participants (36 AD, 23 FTD, 29 CN), 19 channels, 500 Hz, preprocessed derivatives shipped with the dataset (band-pass 0.5-45 Hz, ASR, ICA).

Features. 4-s epochs with 50% overlap; per channel: relative power in delta (0.5-4), theta (4-8), alpha (8-13), beta (13-30) and gamma (30-45 Hz), theta/alpha ratio, normalised spectral entropy; plus the peak alpha frequency. MMSE is not used (all controls score 30).

Models. L2 logistic regression; LightGBM.

Validation. Participant-level: epochs of one person never appear in both training and test folds; 5-fold stratified CV repeated 5 times; each participant's prediction is the mean of their epoch probabilities averaged over repeats; metrics over participants with 1000-sample bootstrap intervals.

Results. AD vs CN AUC 0.91 (0.82-0.97), balanced accuracy 0.81; FTD vs CN AUC 0.83 (0.70-0.94) with LightGBM; AD vs FTD near chance. Comparable to the subject-level studies summarised by the AHEPA benchmark (doi:10.1007/s11571-026-10464-w).

Phase 2. Delta from 1 Hz gives the same results. EEGNet on raw windows (same folds) reaches AUC 0.81 for AD vs CN and 0.64 for FTD vs CN, below the spectral models, because the network overfits with about 60 participants.

Limitations. One small single-centre dataset; no external test set; preprocessing fixed by the dataset authors; power below 2 Hz dominates the relative spectra.

docs.title: Method card: two-sample Mendelian randomisation screen
docs.text:
Question. Which circulating proteins and metabolites have genetic evidence of an effect on Alzheimer's disease risk? The selected molecules are the ones tested later in ADNI proteomics and metabolomics.

Exposures. UKB-PPP plasma proteins, Supplementary Table 9 of Sun et al. 2023 (doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06592-6), cis-pQTL only, MHC excluded. NMR metabolites, Supplementary Table 5 of Karjalainen et al. 2024 (doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07148-y).

Outcome. Alzheimer's disease GWAS of Bellenguez et al. 2022 (doi:10.1038/s41588-022-01024-z, GCST90027158, harmonised file).

Instruments. p < 5e-8; APOE region (chr19:44.4-46.5 Mb, GRCh37) excluded; one variant per 500-kb window (distance-based pruning, an approximation of LD clumping); harmonised on rsID with strand and palindrome checks (palindromes with effect-allele frequency 0.42-0.58 dropped).

Estimators. Wald ratio (one instrument), multiplicative random-effects IVW (two or more), MR-Egger and weighted median as sensitivity analyses (three or more). Benjamini-Hochberg FDR within each exposure family.

Selection for ADNI. FDR < 0.05 and no evidence of directional pleiotropy (Egger intercept p ≥ 0.05 when estimable): 44 proteins and 6 metabolites (Gln, L-VLDL-TG%, M-LDL-FC%, M-LDL-PL%, XS-VLDL-FC, XXL-VLDL-CE%).

Known-answer check. CD33: +0.032 log-odds per SD (0.017-0.047), same direction as the colocalised estimate reported by Zheng et al. 2020 (doi:10.1038/s41588-020-0682-6).

Sensitivity outcome. Kunkle et al. 2019 (no UK Biobank): 42 of the 45 testable selected molecules keep their sign, and 26 of them reach p < 0.05.

Check in ADNI. As a group, the selected molecules do not predict MCI-to-dementia conversion better than other molecules: 48 CSF aptamers among 389 MCI participants, and 6 serum NMR measures among 786. The exception is ACE, with CSF HR 0.76 per SD (p = 0.0006) in the direction predicted by MR. See RESULTS.md.

Colocalisation. coloc ABF on the nine strongest candidates. Seven share the causal variant with AD (PP.H4 > 0.93): CR1, PILRA, PILRB, IL34, C1S, C1R, CD33. ACE and EPHA1 do not under the single-variant assumption. With SuSiE (multiple signals allowed, UK Biobank LD) ACE colocalises through one of five signals (PP.H4 0.98). The MR estimate at that instrument is −0.19 (−0.24 to −0.14). EPHA1 still does not colocalise and is dropped from the credible candidates.

Epitope effects. The instruments of PILRA, IL34, C1S and CD33 are missense, and CR1 has protein-altering proxies, so their pQTLs may partly reflect antibody binding rather than protein amount. ACE (colocalising signal) and C1R are clean.

Limitations. Nearly all proteins have a single cis instrument, so Egger and weighted median cannot be estimated and pleiotropy cannot be tested. Colocalisation covers only nine candidates and assumes one causal variant per region. UK Biobank participants are in both the pQTL study and the AD GWAS (sample overlap), which biases estimates towards the observational association.
